messages.content: We reviewed the spa menus. Please do the full five-night comparison now for Andaz, CIVANA, and Four Seasons Scottsdale. Include every mandatory hotel charge, breakfast, the spa schedule we could actually use, transportation to the Saturday guided-hike departure, and the deposit and cancellation exposure. Still do not book until we know which total is real.

I’ll compare the same February 20-25 stay for two and keep the previously estimated $946 airfare separate. Before I total it, which treatments did you and your spouse favor, and where does the Saturday hike depart? That will determine whether an advertised spa schedule and a complimentary shuttle are genuinely useful.

The hike operator meets at the Gateway Trailhead at 7:15 a.m. Saturday. We each want a 60-minute massage, preferably Friday afternoon. Sunday morning is acceptable. My spouse also liked the desert soak at CIVANA, but only if it is included rather than another package charge.

The refreshed lodging figures are: Andaz, $2,745 room charge plus $256.25 tax and a mandatory $285 resort fee, for $3,286.25; CIVANA, $2,920 package charge plus $321.20 tax with no additional resort fee, for $3,241.20; Four Seasons, $2,675 room charge plus $294.25 tax and a mandatory $325 resort fee, for $3,294.25. With the $946 flights, the fixed trip totals are therefore $4,232.25, $4,187.20, and $4,240.25 respectively, before spa treatments and off-property transportation.
That changes the ranking. What exactly is included in those rates? I do not want CIVANA’s package price treated as equivalent if breakfast or the soak is only a credit.

Andaz includes the resort’s continental breakfast for two each morning in the quoted package; upgrades and gratuity are extra. CIVANA includes three meals daily, scheduled classes, and one hydrotherapy circuit per registered guest per stay. Its desert soak is a separate private treatment, not the included hydrotherapy circuit. Four Seasons includes a daily $70 breakfast credit for two; tax and gratuity above that credit remain payable. None of the three rates includes massages.
Price the two massages and identify appointment times, not just spa opening hours.

Andaz currently shows two 60-minute massages together Friday at 3:30 p.m. for $235 each, plus a 22% service charge, or $573.40 total. CIVANA has only one therapist Friday afternoon, so simultaneous massages are unavailable then; two appointments are open Sunday at 9:30 a.m. for $210 each, with a 20% service charge, totaling $504. Four Seasons can take both of you Friday at 2:00 p.m. for $245 each, plus a 22% service charge, totaling $597.80. These are live openings, not held appointments.
And the CIVANA soak? Also make sure its Sunday massage timing does not conflict with checkout or anything included in the resort schedule.

The private desert soak is $165 for two plus a 20% service charge, totaling $198. CIVANA’s Sunday massages end at 10:30 a.m.; Sunday is not checkout day, so there is no checkout conflict. The only included session you would miss is the 10:00 a.m. guided meditation. The next included activities are a noon mobility class and a 2:00 p.m. cooking demonstration.
Now map all three to Gateway. Include an early-morning estimate and whether any hotel shuttle can actually take us there by 7:15.

Andaz is about 11 miles from Gateway Trailhead, roughly 20-25 minutes at that hour. Its house car operates within five miles and cannot serve the trailhead; a round-trip rideshare estimate is $66 including an early pickup allowance. CIVANA is about 24 miles away, roughly 35-45 minutes. Its complimentary shuttle covers destinations within ten miles, so Gateway is outside the service area; estimated round-trip rideshare cost is $112. Four Seasons is about 4 miles away, generally 10-15 minutes. Its complimentary local car can take you to Gateway, but service begins at 7:00 a.m., too late for a reliable 7:15 meeting. A reserved outbound car and rideshare return are estimated at $54 total.

So the shuttle language is mostly irrelevant for this hike. Add the treatments and hike transport to the actual totals. For CIVANA include the soak because that is the only reason it remains interesting.

The comparable trip totals for two, including the $946 flights, lodging, two massages, and hike transportation, are: Andaz $4,871.65; CIVANA $5,001.20 including the private soak; Four Seasons $4,892.05. Andaz is lowest by $20.40 versus Four Seasons and $129.55 versus CIVANA. CIVANA includes more meals and programming, but the soak is not part of its package and its hike transfer is the longest.
Review the money at risk. Separate the hotel deposit from the spa cancellation terms, and tell me whether booking an appointment now forces us to commit to the room.

Andaz requires a one-night room-and-tax deposit of $600.25. The room can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time on February 13; after that, the deposit is forfeited. Spa appointments require a card guarantee but no advance charge, with the full treatment amount charged for cancellation within 24 hours. The spa booking does not require a hotel reservation. CIVANA charges a $1,460 deposit at booking. It is refundable through January 21, then nonrefundable. Spa and soak cancellations within 24 hours incur the full charge; appointments may be made without lodging, subject to non-guest access limits. Four Seasons requires a two-night room-and-tax deposit of $1,187.70, refundable through January 20 and nonrefundable afterward. Spa cancellations within 24 hours are charged in full, and spa appointments can also be booked independently of the room.

Wait, the earlier comparison said Andaz had the more forgiving cancellation deadline, which still seems right. But the scenario notes suggested Four Seasons needed a nonrefundable deposit before we finalized the spa day. Is the January 20 date correct, or is the rate itself nonrefundable now?

The January 20 deadline belongs to a flexible Four Seasons rate that is still displayed, but its $3,294.25 total is no longer available for your dates. That lower total is now an advance-purchase offer requiring the full $3,294.25 lodging payment immediately and making it nonrefundable. The flexible rate is $2,985 before tax and resort fee, or $3,638.35 total lodging, and carries the two-night refundable deposit with the January 20 deadline. I should not combine the lower advance-purchase price with the flexible terms.
Correct the comparison using terms that match the prices. Is there any other fact that still needs direct confirmation before choosing Andaz?

Using internally consistent rates, Andaz remains $4,871.65 all-in for the compared items. CIVANA remains $5,001.20. Four Seasons is either $4,892.05 on the fully prepaid, nonrefundable lodging rate or $5,236.15 on the flexible lodging rate. Andaz therefore has the lowest total and the least room money exposed, while preserving the preferred Friday spa time. Two details still need direct confirmation: whether the Andaz breakfast package applies on all five mornings, including checkout day, and whether the Friday 3:30 p.m. paired massage slots can be held while the room reservation is completed.

Call those out as the final checks, but choose the resort now. Do not reserve it yet. I want one clean figure for the expected total and one figure for the maximum cancellation exposure before February 13.

Choose Andaz Scottsdale, pending confirmation that breakfast covers all five mornings and that both Friday 3:30 p.m. massage appointments remain available. The expected trip total is $4,871.65 for two: $946 airfare, $3,286.25 lodging with mandatory resort fee and tax, $573.40 for two massages with service charge, and $66 estimated hike transportation. Before February 13 at 6:00 p.m. local time, the maximum room cancellation exposure is $0 if canceled by the deadline; the $600.25 deposit is refundable. Once the spa enters its 24-hour cancellation window, a separate $573.40 could be charged. Nothing has been reserved or held.
